claims.text: Nanoscale chemical ordering is reflected in the average grain size of as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi films.
Nanoscale chemical ordering governs the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of these films.
Chemical ordering and grain size affect magnetocaloric behavior by modulating the nucleation barrier of the magnetostructural transition.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films are in an ordered, single-phase hexagonal state.
The as-deposited films have relatively large, uniform grains.
A controlled thermal anneal can refine the grain structure of the films.
The controlled thermal anneal can introduce modest chemical disorder without causing phase precipitation.
Grain refinement increases the density of grain boundaries.
Grain boundaries act as nucleation sites during the magnetostructural transition.
Increasing the density of grain-boundary nucleation sites produces a distribution of local transformation temperatures.
A distribution of local transformation temperatures broadens or smooths the phase transition.
The coarser-grained as-deposited state has a more uniform and higher nucleation barrier.
The more uniform and higher nucleation barrier in the as-deposited state produces a sharp, strongly hysteretic transition.
Annealed films will exhibit a broader magnetocaloric entropy-change curve than the as-deposited films.
Annealed films will exhibit less magnetocaloric hysteresis than the as-deposited films.
Annealing will somewhat reduce the peak magnetocaloric entropy change.
The predicted behavior is limited to processing conditions that avoid secondary-phase formation and chemical segregation.
Overly aggressive annealing may instead cause unwanted phase changes or grain coarsening.
